docs.title: Q1. What is an exception in Java?
docs.text:
An exception is an event that interrupts the normal flow of program execution.

Example:

`ava int result = 10 / 0; \

This causes ArithmeticException.

⬆ Back to Questions

docs.title: Q2. What is exception handling?
docs.text:
Exception handling is a mechanism used to handle runtime problems without abruptly terminating the application.

⬆ Back to Questions

docs.title: Q3. What is the exception hierarchy?
docs.text:
The root class of Java exceptions and errors is Throwable.

It has two main subclasses:

  • Exception
  • Error

⬆ Back to Questions

docs.title: Q4. Difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?
docs.text:
Checked exceptions are checked by the compiler.

Unchecked exceptions occur at runtime.

⬆ Back to Questions

docs.title: Q5. Difference between throw and throws?
docs.text:
throw explicitly throws an exception.

throws declares possible exceptions in a method signature.

⬆ Back to Questions

docs.title: Q6. How does exception propagation work?
docs.text:
An exception propagates up the call stack until a matching catch block handles it.

⬆ Back to Questions

docs.title: Q7. What is try-with-resources?
docs.text:
It automatically closes resources that implement AutoCloseable.

⬆ Back to Questions

docs.title: Q8. How do you handle exceptions in Spring Boot REST APIs?
docs.text:
Use @RestControllerAdvice and @ExceptionHandler to handle exceptions centrally and return appropriate HTTP status codes and error responses.

docs.title: Java Exception Handling
docs.text:
Understand exception handling from basic to advanced concepts.

Topic

Core Java | Exception Handling | Interview Preparation

docs.title: Q1. What is an exception in Java?
docs.text:
Basic

An exception is an unexpected event that occurs during program execution and interrupts the normal flow of instructions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
public class ExceptionExample {

    public static void main(String[] args) {

        int result = 10 / 0;

        System.out.println(result);
    }
}

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: The above program throws ArithmeticException because integer division by zero is not allowed.

docs.title: Interview Tip
docs.text: Explain that exceptions represent abnormal conditions that an application can handle.

docs.title: Q2. What is exception handling?
docs.text:
Basic

Exception handling is the mechanism used to detect and handle runtime problems so that an application can respond appropriately.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
public class ExceptionHandlingExample {

    public static void main(String[] args) {

        try {
            int result = 10 / 0;
            System.out.println(result);
        } catch (ArithmeticException exception) {
            System.out.println("Cannot divide by zero");
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Interview Tip
docs.text: Explain try, catch, finally, throw and throws.

docs.title: Q3. Why do we need exception handling?
docs.text:
Basic

Exception handling helps applications:

  1. Prevent unexpected termination where recovery is possible.
  2. Maintain application stability.
  3. Separate business logic from error-handling logic.
  4. Provide meaningful error messages.
  5. Support proper logging and debugging.

docs.title: Q4. What is the difference between Exception and Error?
docs.text:
Intermediate

Exception Error Usually represents conditions an application may handle. Usually represents serious system or JVM problems. Can be checked or unchecked. Generally unchecked. Examples: IOException, SQLException. Examples: OutOfMemoryError, StackOverflowError.

docs.title: Q5. Checked vs Unchecked Exceptions
docs.text:
Intermediate

Checked Unchecked Checked at compile time. Not checked at compile time. Must be caught or declared. No mandatory catch or declaration. IOException NullPointerException SQLException ArithmeticException

docs.title: Q6. Java Exception Hierarchy
docs.text:
Advanced

Object
  |
Throwable
  |
  +--- Error
  |
  +--- Exception
         |
         +--- RuntimeException
         |
         +--- IOException
         |
         +--- SQLException

Advanced Interview Tip

Explain Throwable, Exception, RuntimeException and Error with practical examples.
